newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian custom agents to pass on tax to clients.
newsitem.headline: Indian custom agents to pass on tax to clients.

text.p: Indian custom house and steamer agents have accepted a five percent service tax imposed on them, saying they will pass it on to clients, their spokesmen said on Tuesday.

"We are shortly issuing a circular to our members detailing the modalities of collecting the service tax," said Nimesh Shah, vice-president of the Federation of Freight Forwarders' Associations of India.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, in his federal budget for 1997/98 (April/March) unveiled on February 28, proposed a five percent tax on services.
"The tax is not on me. I'll pass it on to my clients," Shah said. A finance ministry statement issued on Friday said the tax will come into effect from June 15.
"The tax will be a burden on trade - importers and exporters. It's for trade to decide what they should do about it," Shah said.
An official of the Indian National Shipowners' Association said the shipping industry had also accepted the service tax.
Ramu Deora, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), said trade had no choice but to accept the service charge.
"We had pleaded with the finance ministry to lift the tax. But our demand had been rejected," Deora said.
In early April, nearly 2.2 million truck operators went on a strike for 10 days in protest against the five percent service tax, paralysing India's foreign trade.
The government had to postpone its decision on imposing the five percent service tax on the transport sector.
"We have not taken any decision on it yet," said a finance ministry official on Friday.
